reason: Both lose the dark brand header (the SOLSTICE logo shrinks to an illegible speck at top-left), and both keep the paragraph body copy and the long legal block at unreadable sizes, so the legal text weighs as much as the message in a cramped strip. A drops the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow but keeps a cleaner left/centre/right order: copy, then headline over CTA, then legal. B moves the eyebrow to the bottom-right under the legal text, which breaks the reading order and muddles hierarchy. B's body copy is also squeezed into ragged, awkward wrapping.

A reads cleanly left to right (sale ribbon, then a dominant headline, then a strong CTA), but it drops the product can and the Solstice logo, the red ribbon is crammed tiny into the top-left corner, and the legal line under the headline can't be read. B keeps the product and logo, but it puts a 4-line block of legal text at the far left where it competes with the headline as a second focal point, and it shrinks the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon to a tiny strip under the headline, so the left side looks cluttered and the hierarchy is muddled.

A breaks the button away from its headline: the 'See the Flavours' pill is pushed into the far-right corner, almost touching the edge. That leaves a big empty band across the middle. The headline wraps in a ragged way, with 'Bubbles,' on its own line, and the small, distant button no longer reads as the next step after the headline. B is basically a shrunk copy of the original, centred with large empty orange areas on both sides, and the button label is tiny. Still, the headline-to-button order and grouping are intact and the line breaks match the original, so it is coherent but not a real redesign for the wide format.

A keeps the headline and subline at readable sizes, with Try It as a clear CTA. But the NEW badge has shrunk to an illegible sticker that collides with the top edge of the button, and the product can is reduced to a tiny, unrecognisable blob. B keeps the original's left-to-right order with a separate NEW pill, but the subline is shrunk to illegible micro-type, the can is just as tiny, and the oversized empty NEW pill competes with the CTA. A is slightly less broken because its key copy stays readable.

Both cram the whole poster into a 320x50 strip: the body copy and legal block become illegible micro-text, the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow sits below the legal text at bottom right (wrong reading order), and the logo is a barely visible speck. The headline and CTA in the centre hold up in both. A keeps the body copy to a tidier 3-line block. B wraps it into about 6 lines that run nearly from the top edge to the bottom edge, leaving the left column more cramped and ragged.

A is just a scaled-down copy of the leaderboard: the subline shrinks to about 7px and can't be read, and the large NEW pill sits in empty space, about as heavy as the small 'Try It' CTA. B makes the headline and subline readable and tucks NEW onto the CTA as a badge, but the badge is cramped against the top edge and overlaps the button, the product circle is cropped top and bottom, and the subline runs right up to the CTA with no gutter.

Both candidates are poor. A keeps the logo and puts the orange CTA high on the left, so the order reads brand, then action, then headline. But the body copy runs off the right edge, where it is clipped and cramped, and 'Ships late June', the logo and the button are crowded into a narrow left column. B is a large headline block with no visible logo, and the brand header band is gone. The CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill at the bottom, buried beside the legal line. The body copy is squeezed into a narrow column on the right that is too small to read, and 'Ships late June' floats in the bottom-left corner on its own.

A shrinks the product bottle to a tiny speck in the bottom-right, away from its cream circle, which now sits empty bottom-left. The headline is also off the centre axis that NEW and Try It share, leaving big dead areas and a lost hero image. B keeps the bottle large and reads left to right (headline, bottle, then NEW and CTA), but its cream backing circle is also an orphaned empty disc bottom-left, the headline sits almost against the bottle, and NEW is detached high above the CTA.

A keeps the bottle as a strong focal point and the headline readable, but the bottle has lost its cream circle backdrop: that circle now sits on its own in the bottom-left corner, with a faint stray circle top-left. The bottle also crowds the end of the headline, and the NEW/Try It column on the right floats loosely. B shrinks the bottle to an icon-sized speck in the bottom-right, which loses the key product image. It also leaves the orphaned cream circle bottom-left and centres the headline slightly off-axis from the NEW pill and CTA, with large dead areas, so it reads as a sparse, unintentional layout.

A: the sage circle now sits on its own behind the headline instead of framing the product, GROVE falls below the headline, the product floats in a big empty middle, and the CTA, badges and FREE DELIVERY are shrunk into a small cluster near the bottom, so the CTA is tiny and buried. B: the CTA and badges are crammed into the top-left corner above the headline, and the circle collides with them. That flips the reading order, makes the CTA tiny, and leaves the bottom third as dead space. A keeps a more sensible headline → product → action order, so it is the less bad of the two.

A: SOLSTICE sits below the headline, which breaks the reading order. The 'Find It Near You' CTA is shrunk to the size of the badges, and the CTA and two pills wrap into a ragged cluster with SUMMER ONLY on its own line. The headline sits on the green circle, which has come loose from the phone, and the phone is pushed far right with dead space between them. B: SOLSTICE now comes before the headline, and the big headline keeps a clear hierarchy. But the phone almost touches the end of 'back', the CTA is again a tiny pill the size of the badges, SUMMER ONLY is orphaned far below the other pills, and the circle has moved behind the text instead of framing the phone. B is less bad because its brand-then-headline order and hierarchy hold up better.

A gets the order wrong: the SOLSTICE wordmark sits below the headline and is set almost as large as it. The two badges are blown up to button size, so they read as two more CTAs under 'Find It Near You'. The bottom badge also sits on a stray green circle fragment, and there is a big empty band at the top. B keeps brand → headline → phone in the right order, with a large phone and subordinate badges. But its bottom is badly jammed: the tagline, CTA and both badges are stacked with almost no gaps, the CTA pill nearly touches both side edges, and the badges sit on a leftover circle fragment, all below a very tall phone, so the layout is lopsided.

A: the headline runs over the empty cream circle, so 'Blood' is white-on-cream and hard to read. The bottle has drifted out of its circle to sit beside the headline, and the NEW badge is jammed on top of the Try It button, so the result looks broken. B keeps the original structure, with the bottle in its circle, the headline, and the CTA on the right edge, and nothing collides. Its flaws: the NEW badge is tiny and floats under the headline instead of sitting near the CTA, the bottle is very small, and the Try It button is cramped against the right edge.

A: the attribution 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' is set bolder and nearly as large as the quote, so the hierarchy is inverted. The hero can has shrunk to a speck inside the circle and the SOLSTICE logo is effectively gone, which loses the product and the brand. B keeps the quote dominant and readable and keeps the can at a good size, but the logo is a tiny illegible fragment floating mid-canvas. The attribution is shrunk to unreadable fine print and pushed to the bottom edge, far from its quote, and the oversized quote mark eats the top.

A reads cleanly left to right (logo, shoe, headline with subline, badge), but the lime circle is split off from the shoe and cropped at the right edge, and the NEW VIDEO badge sits on that orphaned circle far from the content. B is worse: the logo is jammed against the top edge, the shoe is clipped at the top and pulled away from its circle, and 'Full review inside.' breaks onto two cramped lines squeezed between the shoe and the circle.

A: the elements float at unrelated heights. The headline is vertically centred, the CTA sits high on the right, and the fine print is stranded at the bottom right, far below the CTA and not aligned with it. The oversized phone in the middle competes with the headline. B is a coherent left-to-right row with the fine print grouped under the headline. Its flaws are a phone shrunk to a minor icon, which weakens the key imagery, a large dead gap between the headline and the CTA, and an undersized CTA.

A reads left to right as a banner should, with a clear headline. But the 'Find It Near You' CTA is tiny, no bigger than the two badges, and buried in a row of three pills; the body copy is squeezed into a narrow 5-line column; and the can is shrunk to an icon. B has more serious problems: the can and circle are cropped off the left edge; the SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline; the body copy is tiny; the CTA and badges form a ragged, cramped stack on the far right; and a big empty gap sits in the middle.

A: the green circle has come off the phone and now sits behind the headline. The headline breaks badly, leaving 'back' alone on its own line. The subcopy wraps awkwardly, and the small CTA is stacked in with two badges of about the same size, so it gets lost; the right-hand column is cramped while the lower left is empty. B: the phone and circle stay together, but the SOLSTICE wordmark has dropped below the headline, so the reading order is wrong. The two badges have grown to the full size of the CTA, which flattens the hierarchy, and the headline is jammed against the top edge. Even so, B is more coherent than A.

A pushes the whole block right, leaving the left third empty. Its headline is shrunk to barely above body size with a single orphaned word ('sunshine.') on the second line, and the centred headline clashes with the left-aligned CTA, so the type has no shared axis. B keeps a dominant two-line headline that reads left to right like a banner, but its subcopy is squeezed into a narrow five-line column with ragged breaks. That column sits almost against the headline's period, and the CTA is jammed against the bottom-right edge with no margin.

A breaks the reading order: the SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline. The flavour pills are a jumbled 2+1 cluster with mismatched sizes (the BLOOD ORANGE label is much smaller than the others), and the headline column is pushed right, leaving the top-left as dead space with only the circles. B keeps the wordmark, headline, copy and CTA in the original order on a clean left edge, with three even pills in one row. It still needs fixes: there is a large dead gap between the headline and the subcopy, the pill order is reversed from the original, the BLOOD ORANGE pill crowds the right edge over the peach circle, and the wordmark sits on top of the yellow circle.

A keeps 'Sunset Sessions' clearly dominant on the left, but the tagline is squeezed into a four-line sliver, 'Saturday 21 / June' breaks awkwardly, the RSVP CTA has shrunk to a pill the same size as the badges, and the large missing-asset placeholder eats the right third. B has a jumbled reading order: 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' sits at the very bottom, the date comes before the tagline, and the left edges of the text lines are ragged. Its logo is nearly invisible, the CTA is likewise reduced to a badge, and the placeholder plus fine print crowd the top-left, so the hierarchy is weaker than in A.

A keeps the original two-column structure and the phone, but the SOLSTICE wordmark now sits below the headline, the headline is jammed against the top edge, and the two badges have been inflated into full-width pills the same size as the CTA. 'SUMMER ONLY' in bright orange actually outweighs 'Find It Near You', so the call to action no longer stands out. B has a stronger headline, but it breaks into three lines with 'back' left alone on the last one, and the green circle floats behind the text, detached from the phone. Its subcopy leaves 'sweet.' alone on a line, the CTA and badges shrink to tiny stacked pills (with 'BACK BYDEMAND' missing a space), and the right column is cramped while the lower left is empty. B is the less coherent resize.

A scrambles the reading order: 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' drops to the bottom, the tagline sits under the date and the venue sits under the URL. It also puts the large grey missing-asset placeholder and the legal text in the top-centre spot, shrinks the logo to a speck, lets the oversized phone take over the left side, and turns the RSVP CTA into a pill the same size as the badges. B at least keeps the headline dominant on the left and the logo on its circle, but it has clear breaks: the tagline is squeezed into a 4-line column, 'Saturday 21 June' leaves 'June' orphaned, the phone is tiny, RSVP is again just one of four equal pills, and the legal text and the large placeholder sit loose in the middle.

A rearranges for the tall format: the can, the full-width headline and the CTA are all a good size, and the copy sits in a tight group. But the SOLSTICE wordmark has been moved under the headline, which breaks the original's brand-first reading order, and the top ~130px is empty. B keeps the order but shrinks everything: the can is small, the body copy is about 11px and hard to read, and the CTA is undersized. It also leaves large dead gaps between the can, the headline, the body and the button, so it reads as a scaled-down copy rather than a redesign.

A: the headline sits right on the olive circle and wraps to leave 'fizz' orphaned on its own line. The 'Find a Store' CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill crammed against the bottom edge, which buries the action, and the bottom is jammed while the pack takes up most of the height. B: the CITRINE wordmark has moved below the headline, which breaks the brand-first reading order. The CTA is oversized and sits after a large dead gap. Even so, the headline is on one line, the text is clear of the circles, and the hierarchy is legible, so B is the less broken of the two.

A keeps a readable CTA and a sensible headline/CTA hierarchy. But the whole group is pushed right, leaving the left third as dead orange space. The centred headline sits jammed near the top edge, and the CTA is left-aligned under it, so the two share no clean axis. B's headline is oversized and crammed against the left, top and bottom edges. Its CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill with near-illegible text, wedged against the right edge, so the call to action is effectively buried.

A is basically a shrunk copy of the original: the can, subcopy and 'Find a Store' button are all small, the subcopy is close to unreadable at this size, the SOLSTICE wordmark sits half on the edge of the green circle, and there is a big empty gap between the can and the headline. B scales the can, headline and CTA up well for the tall format, but it moves the SOLSTICE wordmark from the top to between the headline and subcopy, which breaks the reading order and how the brand is shown, and it leaves the top-left corner empty.

A: the teal circle has come away from the can and now sits behind the 'Cucumber Mint is back' headline, which breaks the product's look and puts text over a graphic. The 'Find It Near You' CTA has shrunk to a small pill no bigger than the badges, and the three columns feel scattered. B: the can stays inside its circle and the design is recognisable, but 'GLACIER' now sits under the headline (wrong reading order), the CTA is a tiny pill the same size as the badges, 'SUMMER ONLY' wraps onto its own line, and the text stack is cramped above a large empty strip at the bottom.

A gets the reading order backwards: the CTA and LIMITED badge are crammed into the top-left corner against the canvas edge, above the headline. That leaves a big dead band between them and the headline, which sits low with an orphan-like 'Bubbles,' line. B keeps headline then CTA in the right order and centres the headline well. Its flaws: the CTA is small and pushed to the left, the LIMITED pill floats off on its own at the right instead of sitting next to the button, the button row is off the headline's centre axis, and the bottom third is empty.

A: the reading order is broken. The SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline and is set large enough to compete with it. The Blood Orange pill lands on the column of legal text on the left, and the other two pills are split above and below the Shop Flavours button, so the three flavour pills are scattered across both ends of the banner. B: the structure is sensible (headline on the left, CTA in the centre, flavour pills grouped top right) and the headline and CTA lead clearly. Its flaws: the SOLSTICE logo has shrunk to an almost invisible size above the button, the subhead is tiny and wraps awkwardly beside the pills, the legal line is jammed right under the button, and the right-hand cluster is cramped.

A: the phone is small and centred while the headline and subcopy sit flush left, but the CTA is centred, so the elements share no common axis. The 'Online Only' badge floats alone in the top-left, the headline is undersized for a square, and there are big dead gaps between the text lines, plus a cropped cream circle in the corner. B: the two-column layout (large phone left, copy right) keeps the original's reading order and gives the product proper weight. However, the CTA is not aligned with the text's left edge, the badge is stranded near the bottom away from the CTA, the headline is still small, the top band is empty and the cream circle is clipped. B is the less bad of the two.

A: the headline fills the full banner height and leaves no room, the CTA is jammed against the top-right corner, the CITRINE logo is shrunk to an illegible speck under the button, and the product pack is a tiny, unreadable thumbnail. B reads cleanly from left to right (product, then headline over a legible CITRINE wordmark, then CTA), but the pack is still a tiny thumbnail, the decorative circles and their brand colours are gone, and the wordmark now sits under the headline instead of above it, which flips the original order.

The two layouts are nearly the same, and both share the same flaws. The 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow has dropped below the subhead, which breaks the original reading order. The top area above the headline is empty, there is a large dead gap between the shoe and the CTA, and the legal line is tiny. B is slightly worse: its legal text wraps onto two lines and leaves 'responsibly.' alone on the second line. That left-aligned block is also off-centre under a centred button. A keeps the legal on one line, and its spacing at the top is a little tighter.

A looks like the original banner stretched vertically: the headline, subcopy and LIMITED badge are spread apart with large uneven gaps, the CTA floats alone at the right edge with no link to the copy, and the shoe and text don't share a vertical centre, leaving the lower half empty. B groups the headline, subcopy and CTA into one compact block next to a larger shoe, which gives clearer hierarchy. However, the LIMITED badge sits off to the right of the CTA on no clear axis, the content block is crowded into the upper-middle with a dead bottom third, and the CTA is smaller than in the original.

A: the GLACIER wordmark sits under the headline, which flips the brand-to-message order. The SOLSTICE can is shrunk to a tiny sliver jammed against the right edge after the CTA. The legal copy is an unreadable grey smudge crammed between the headline and the button. B: the reading order is better (brand and can on the left, headline in the centre, CTA on the right), but the headline breaks onto a second line that holds only the orphan word 'fizz'. The can is a tiny icon, the CTA presses against the top edge, and the legal text under it is illegible.

A: the teal circle has come apart from the can, so the can sits on the circle's top edge. The 'Find It Near You' CTA has shrunk to a pill no bigger than the badges, and 'SUMMER ONLY' wraps onto a ragged second line. The GLACIER wordmark sits below the headline, and the bottom-right half of the canvas is empty. B is worse: the CTA and badges are pushed into the top-left corner as tiny pills and read as a header, not the action. The can is small and floats on its own, and the detached circle sits behind the headline, the GLACIER wordmark and the body copy, an unintended collision. The bottom third is empty.

A is a coherent left-to-right banner: bottle, then a cleanly left-aligned text block, then the CTA. Its flaws: the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow is demoted below the body copy, the bottle nearly touches the top and bottom edges, and there is a wide dead gap between the copy and the CTA. B's text is scattered: the eyebrow is stranded top-left, the '20% off' headline sits low at the bottom-left, and the subcopy floats mid-height on its own baseline with no shared alignment. The bottle is also jammed against the Shop Sale button, leaving the right side cramped and the centre empty.

A: 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' sits below the subtitle and URL, so the reading order is out of sequence. RSVP has been shrunk to the same pill as the three tags, so the CTA is buried, and the logo is a tiny fragment under the decorative circle; the headline and phone still read cleanly left to right. B: the headline has strong hierarchy, but the right half is a cramped jumble (stray subtitle and time fragments, a tiny RSVP squeezed into the tag row, illegible legal text). A large grey placeholder box also becomes a dominant focal point, so B is the messier of the two.

Both lose the hero: the Quillbrook bag shrinks to a tiny thumbnail beside the logo, and an empty blurred brown box takes its place. A at least keeps headline, copy and CTA together in a clear top-down order, though the SAVE 15% badge is bigger than the CTA and the logo is buried at the bottom. B is worse: the CTA shrinks to a small button jammed into the bottom-left corner below an oversized badge, there is a dead gap at the top, and the empty image block dominates the canvas.

Both lose the hero coffee bag: it shrinks to a tiny thumbnail beside the logo, leaving an empty blurred-brown box where the product should be. A is worse. Its CTA is a tiny pill crammed into the bottom-left corner with the bag and logo, the SAVE 15% badge is bigger than the CTA, and the top band is empty. B at least keeps the CTA directly under the copy, though it is centred while the text is left-aligned and it is still smaller than the badge.
